lead.t: Hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) is a functional, rapidly progressive renal failure that occurs in patients with advanced chronic liver disease (usually cirrhosis) or acute severe liver injury, in the absence of intrinsic kidney pathology.

b: Renal failure in severe liver disease WITHOUT intrinsic kidney disease - Excluded: concomitant liver + kidney damage, ATN secondary to circulatory collapse - Pathogenesis: vasoconstriction → decreased renal blood flow - Urine : hyperosmolar

| Hepatorenal syndrome – type 1 | Rapid creatinine rise, advanced cirrhosis, precipitating infection | No intrinsic renal pathology, FeNa <1 %, no casts |
Signs of chronic liver disease (spider naevi, palmar erythema): May coexist with hepatorenal syndrome in advanced disease.

qs.q: Which clinical feature is characteristic of Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS) occurring in patients with cirrhosis?
o: Elevated urine sodium greater than 40 mmol/L
Intrinsic structural renal disease on biopsy
qs.e: Hepatorenal syndrome is characterized by a low urine sodium of less than 10 mmol/L, normal intravascular volume, and the absence of intrinsic renal disease. A high urine sodium would point toward acute tubular necrosis rather than HRS.

qs.q: What is recognized as the only definitive cure for Hepatorenal Syndrome (HRS)?
qs.e: Liver transplantation is noted as the only definitive cure for hepatorenal syndrome, although vasoactive agents and TIPS can be used as bridging or supportive measures. Diuretics are typically withdrawn.

qs.q: Which finding is typically observed in the urine of a patient suffering from hepatorenal syndrome?
o: Hyperosmolar and protein-negative with low sodium
Hypoosmolar with massive proteinuria and high sodium
Isosthenuric with active hematuria and cellular casts
Alkaline with prominent glucosuria and bilirubinuria
qs.e: Hepatorenal syndrome presents with functional renal failure where urine is characteristically hyperosmolar, protein-negative, and low in sodium due to intense renal vasoconstriction. Intrinsic kidney damage or acute tubular necrosis are excluded.
